title: Monitoring progress and delay in labour
blurb: Record first-stage observations on a partogram, recognise transfer triggers, and manage delay in the first and second stages under NICE NG235.
question: Jess, in her first labour at an alongside midwifery unit, was 5 cm at 10:00 and is 6 cm at 14:00 with intact membranes. She and her baby are well. What should the midwife do now, and what happens if progress stays slow?

teach.body: Formally: NICE NG235 requires regular maternal and fetal observations in the first stage, an hourly risk assessment, a partogram once labour is established, and set definitions of delay with stepwise interventions. In plain English: the midwife keeps a running picture of how the woman and baby are and how labour is progressing, intervenes only when progress or wellbeing changes, and moves care to obstetric-led when the triggers are met.

How often
rows: Offer 4-hourly, or if concern or she wishes
Risk assessment of woman and baby
teach.caption: Use a partogram once labour is established (NG235 1.8.22).

head: Observation
Trigger
rows: Diastolic 90+ or systolic 140+ twice, 15–30 min apart
Under 9 or over 21, twice 15–30 min apart
Fresh bleeding, new meconium, unusual pain, confirmed delay, epidural request
teach.caption: Fetal triggers include non-cephalic presentation, a high head in a first labour, suspected FGR or macrosomia and FHR changes (NG235 1.8.20).

teach.h: Delay in the established first stage

steps.label: Suspect delay
steps.sub: under 2 cm in 4 h (or slowing in later labours)

steps.label: Support and discuss
steps.sub: hydration, pain relief; VE in 2 h

teach.caption: Do not advise transfer to obstetric-led care for amniotomy alone (NG235 1.8.47).

rows.label: Dose increases
rows.tag: No more often than every 30 minutes

rows.label: VE 4 h after regular contractions
rows.tag: Under 2 cm progress: review for caesarean

teach.note: Do not start separate IV fluids without a clinical indication; monitor fluid balance.

rows.label: Senior review if not imminent after

teach.caption: No progress at reassessment: offer VE, consider amniotomy if membranes intact; still no progress: diagnose delay, senior review (NG235 1.9.25–1.9.28).

teach.body: Encourage drinking to thirst (isotonic drinks may help) but no more than normal: overconsumption can cause hyponatraemia (sodium under 130 mmol/L) with maternal and neonatal seizures. Monitor fluid balance with IV fluids, oxytocin, poor output or medical conditions. A positive balance of 1,500 mL or more, or signs of hyponatraemia, needs obstetric review, a sodium test and transfer from a midwifery setting. Review bladder care at least every 4 hours.

Jess has progressed 1 cm in 4 hours, so delay is suspected. The midwife discusses the findings, offers support, fluids and effective pain relief, and advises a VE in 2 hours. At 16:00 she is 6.5 cm: under 1 cm, so delay is diagnosed. With consent the midwife performs an amniotomy in the midwifery unit, explaining it shortens labour by about an hour and may make contractions stronger. If there is no progress 2 hours later, she transfers Jess to obstetric-led care.

teach.text: Two different numbers: delay is SUSPECTED at under 2 cm in 4 hours, but DIAGNOSED at under 1 cm on the VE 2 hours later. And amniotomy alone is not a reason to transfer.

items: Contractions half-hourly; pulse hourly; temperature, BP and RR 4-hourly; VE offered 4-hourly.
Partogram once labour is established; hourly risk assessment.
Suspect delay under 2 cm in 4 h; diagnose under 1 cm in 2 h; consider amniotomy.
Oxytocin: epidural offered first, increments no more often than every 30 min, 3 to 4 in 10.
Second stage: nulliparous within 3 h, multiparous within 2 h; senior review at 2 h and 1 h of pushing.
Positive fluid balance 1,500 mL: obstetric review and sodium check.

summary: You can now carry out and record first-stage observations, recognise maternal and fetal transfer triggers, and manage suspected and confirmed delay. You can also apply the oxytocin rules, the second-stage time frames and the fluid balance safeguards in NICE NG235.

A.q: When should a midwife start a partogram for a woman in labour?
options: At the first triage telephone call
From the start of the latent phase
Once she reaches full dilatation
Once labour is established
A.why: NG235 1.8.22: use a pictorial record of labour (partogram) once labour is established.

whyNot.0: Triage calls are documented, but the partogram starts in established labour.
whyNot.1: The latent phase is not plotted on the partogram.
whyNot.2: Starting at full dilatation would miss the first stage.

A.q: How often should the woman's pulse be recorded in the established first stage of labour?
options: Every 15 minutes
Hourly
Every 4 hours
Every 30 minutes
A.why: NG235 1.8.19: record hourly pulse during the first stage.

whyNot.0: Every 15 minutes is not the routine first-stage interval.
whyNot.2: 4-hourly applies to temperature, BP and respiratory rate.

A.q: Which temperature finding in the first stage is a trigger for transfer to obstetric-led care?
options: 37.5°C or above on a single reading
38.5°C or above on a single reading
37.5°C or above twice, 1 hour apart
37.2°C or above twice, 1 hour apart
A.why: NG235 1.8.20: temperature of 38°C or above on a single reading, or 37.5°C or above on 2 consecutive occasions 1 hour apart.

whyNot.0: A single reading of 37.5°C is not itself a trigger.
whyNot.1: The single-reading trigger is 38°C, so this is too high a threshold.
whyNot.3: The repeat-reading threshold is 37.5°C, so 37.2°C twice is not a trigger.

B.q: Delay in Ama's established first stage is suspected. She and her baby are well. What should the midwife advise next?
options: A VE in 2 hours; delay if under 1 cm
Start an oxytocin infusion now
Transfer to the obstetric unit for amniotomy
A VE in 4 hours; delay if under 2 cm
B.why: NG235 1.8.45: advise a vaginal examination 2 hours later and diagnose delay if progress is less than 1 cm.

whyNot.1: Oxytocin follows obstetric review for confirmed delay, not suspected delay.
whyNot.2: Transfer is not advised for amniotomy alone.
whyNot.3: The repeat VE is at 2 hours, with a 1 cm threshold.

B.q: Delay is diagnosed in the first stage for Jess at an alongside midwifery unit. Her membranes are intact and there are no other concerns. What is most appropriate?
options: Transfer her to the obstetric unit for amniotomy
Start oxytocin within the midwifery unit
Consider amniotomy without transferring her
Wait 4 more hours before any intervention
B.why: NG235 1.8.46–1.8.47: consider amniotomy if membranes are intact, after explanation; do not advise transfer to obstetric-led care for amniotomy alone.

whyNot.0: Amniotomy alone is not a reason to transfer.
whyNot.1: Oxytocin is an obstetric-led intervention after obstetric review.
whyNot.3: Delay has been diagnosed; waiting 4 hours is not the NG235 step.

B.q: Grace is on an oxytocin infusion for delay. How often may the dose be increased?
options: Every 10 minutes until contractions are regular
Every 15 minutes until contractions are regular
Every 20 minutes until contractions are regular
No more often than every 30 minutes
B.why: NG235 1.8.54: the time between increments should be no more frequent than every 30 minutes, increasing until 3 to 4 contractions in 10 minutes.

whyNot.0: 10-minute increments are too frequent and risk hyperstimulation.

C.q: On oxytocin, Zara is having 5 contractions in 10 minutes. The CTG is normal. What should the midwife do?
options: Continue the rate and recheck in 30 minutes
Reduce or stop until 4 or fewer in 10
Give a fluid bolus and continue the rate
Stop it and do not restart in this labour
C.why: NG235 1.8.55: if contractions are more frequent than 4 in 10 minutes, reduce or stop oxytocin until there are 4 or fewer in 10 minutes.

whyNot.0: Continuing risks hyperstimulation and fetal hypoxia.
whyNot.2: Fluids do not treat excessive contraction frequency; NG235 says reduce or stop.
whyNot.3: Oxytocin can be restarted after review if appropriate (NG235 1.8.57).

C.q: Priya, in her first labour without an epidural, has pushed actively for 1 hour. There is no descent or rotation. Her membranes are intact. What should the midwife do?
options: Offer a VE and consider amniotomy
Encourage pushing for 2 more hours
Diagnose delay and start oxytocin
Advise directed pushing lying flat
C.why: NG235 1.9.25: after 1 hour of active pushing with no signs of progress, offer a vaginal examination and consider amniotomy if the membranes are intact; if still no progress, diagnose delay and escalate.

whyNot.1: Continuing without reassessment ignores the 1-hour review point.
whyNot.2: Oxytocin in the second stage follows obstetric assessment after transfer.
whyNot.3: Lying flat on her back can reduce placental blood flow.

C.q: Mina, multiparous with an epidural, has pushed actively for 1 hour and birth is not imminent. What should the midwife do?
options: Encourage her to continue pushing for a further hour
Start an oxytocin infusion to strengthen contractions
Refer for senior review of place and mode of birth
Advise her to stop pushing and rest for an hour
C.why: NG235 1.9.28: for a multiparous woman with an epidural, if birth is not imminent after 1 hour of pushing, refer for senior review and a decision on place and mode of birth.

whyNot.0: The 1-hour point for multiparous women requires senior review.
whyNot.1: Oxytocin is not used routinely in the second stage with an epidural (NG235 1.6.35).
whyNot.3: Stopping pushing delays the review she needs.

reteach.title: Suspect, check, act
reteach.question: Think of delay as three questions asked 2 hours apart. What is checked each time, and what is the action?

blocks.body: 4 hours: has she dilated at least 2 cm? If not, suspect delay, support her and recheck. 2 hours later: at least 1 cm more? If not, delay is diagnosed; consider amniotomy where she is. 2 hours after amniotomy: any progress? If not, transfer for obstetric review and consideration of oxytocin.

blocks.text: Oxytocin rules: every 30 minutes at most, aim for 3 to 4 in 10, stop at once if the CTG is pathological.

explain.body: Half-hourly contraction frequency, hourly pulse, 4-hourly temperature, BP and respiratory rate, 4-hourly VE offered, and an hourly risk assessment.

test.q: How often should contraction frequency be documented in the first stage of labour?
options: Hourly
Every 4 hours
Every 15 minutes
Half-hourly
test.why: NG235 1.8.19: half-hourly documentation of the frequency of contractions.

whyNot.0: Hourly is the interval for pulse.
whyNot.1: 4-hourly is for temperature, BP and respiratory rate.
whyNot.2: Every 15 minutes is not the NG235 interval.

explain.body: Maternal triggers include pulse over 120 twice, severe or persistent hypertension, abnormal respiratory rate, fever, bleeding, new meconium, unusual pain and confirmed delay. Fetal triggers include FHR changes and non-cephalic presentation.

test.q: Which finding in the first stage is a trigger for transfer to obstetric-led care?
options: Pulse 125 on two readings 20 minutes apart
Pulse 115 on two readings 20 minutes apart
BP 138/88 on two readings 20 minutes apart
Temperature 37.6°C on a single reading
test.why: NG235 1.8.20: maternal pulse over 120 beats a minute on 2 occasions 15 to 30 minutes apart.

whyNot.3: A single 37.6°C reading is below the single-reading trigger of 38°C.

explain.body: Advise a VE 4 hours after oxytocin has produced regular contractions in established labour. Under 2 cm progress: further obstetric review about caesarean birth. 2 cm or more: 4-hourly VEs.

test.q: Four hours after oxytocin produced regular contractions, Tara's cervix has dilated by 1 cm. What does NICE NG235 advise?
options: Continue with 4-hourly vaginal examinations
Obstetric review about a caesarean birth
Increase the oxytocin and recheck in 4 hours
Stop the oxytocin and allow a rest period
test.why: NG235 1.8.58: if dilatation has increased by less than 2 cm after 4 hours of oxytocin, further obstetric review is needed to assess whether caesarean birth is advisable.

whyNot.0: 4-hourly VEs follow progress of 2 cm or more.
whyNot.2: This repeats an approach that has not worked, without review.
whyNot.3: This does not address the need for obstetric review.

explain.body: Monitor fluid balance with IV fluids, oxytocin, output concerns or conditions such as pre-eclampsia. Positive balance of 1,500 mL or more, or signs of hyponatraemia: explain, obstetric review, sodium test, and transfer from a midwifery setting.

test.q: Kim's fluid balance in labour is positive by 1,600 mL. What should the midwife do?
options: Encourage her to drink more isotonic drinks
Start IV fluids to treat her ketonuria
Request obstetric review and a sodium test
Continue care and recheck the balance in 4 hours
test.why: NG235 1.8.28: with a positive fluid balance of 1,500 mL or more, explain possible hyponatraemia, request obstetric review, offer a sodium test and transfer if in a midwifery-led setting.

whyNot.0: More fluid would worsen the risk of hyponatraemia.
whyNot.1: Ketonuria in women without diabetes is not treated with fluids (NG235 1.8.29).
whyNot.3: This delays review of possible hyponatraemia.
